Environmental Studies • Circular Textile Concept

Waste is the
New Raw Material.

RE-FIBRE is a conceptual circular textile system that explores how unwanted garments can be collected, identified, sorted and processed into material for new products.

01 / THE PROBLEM

Fast fashion is a linear system.

Rapid production and short garment use cycles increase pressure on resources and contribute to pollution and textile waste.

💧

Resource Depletion

Textile production requires raw materials, water and energy. Synthetic fibres are commonly derived from fossil-based feedstocks.

RESOURCE PRESSURE
🧪

Pollution

Textile production and use can involve dyes, wastewater, emissions and fibre shedding that place pressure on environmental systems.

POLLUTION
♻️

Textile Waste

When unwanted clothing is discarded instead of being reused or recovered, valuable material can leave the productive cycle.

MATERIAL LOSS

07 / MATERIAL TO PRODUCT

Recovered textile material can re-enter different product cycles.

01 • FIBRE

Recovered textile fibres become the starting material.

02 • YARN / MATERIAL

Depending on composition and technology, fibres can be processed into new textile material.

03 • PRODUCTS

Potential applications include apparel, bags, cushions and accessories.

04 • INTERIORS

Potential interior applications include upholstery, rugs and acoustic textile panels.

RE-FIBRE

Waste is the New Raw Material.

An Environmental Studies project exploring fast fashion, resource depletion, pollution, textile waste and a conceptual circular recovery system.

RE-FIBRE is presented as a conceptual prototype. Material recovery outcomes depend on actual fibre composition, contamination and available recycling technologies.
